name: Ash Amrani
role: Data archaeologist recovering pre-Collapse digital records and reconstructing lost histories
location: The Circuit, operating out of a rented server-adjacent lab space in Deepwell Station, near sub-level access near LaSalle and Congress
description:
Ash Amrani is slight and pale in the way of someone who has spent formative years in low-light server environments, with Lithuanian-Nigerian heritage that shows in his long jaw and the particular amber tone of his skin under fluorescent lab lights. He has bioluminescent lines running along his temples and the back of his hands — a geneware mod he got at nineteen and has never regretted, pale blue-white that brightens when he's concentrating and dims when he sleeps. His hair is a dark loose cloud that he ties back with whatever cable is nearest. He looks younger than he is, which he has stopped trying to correct; instead he uses the underestimation strategically.

He is possessed by the specific obsession of the archivist: not just what is lost, but the shape of what is lost, the way a gap in the record is itself a record. He can spend eight hours in pursuit of a single corrupted timestamp. He is not antisocial — he can be delightful company, quick-witted and genuinely curious — but he disappears into his work in a way that has cost him two relationships and the trust of a department head who needed him to surface for funding reviews.

core_fears: That the records he recovers will be used to harm the descendants of the people in them
That he will finish his life's work and it will not matter to anyone
core_desires: To recover the complete pre-Collapse residential history of what is now the Shelf, restoring named personhood to erased communities
To find proof of a specific corporate data-destruction event he suspects happened in the 2140s
coping_mechanisms: Immersion in work to the exclusion of everything else
Maintains an elaborate personal ritual of leaving audio logs for 'future archivists' to find — a practice he knows is irrational and continues anyway
blind_spots: Does not adequately consider that some data was deliberately destroyed by the people it was about, to protect themselves — he reads all deletion as loss
psychology.secret: He has already found fragmentary evidence of the 2140s Arcturus data-destruction event he theorizes about. He has not published because he is terrified the evidence is too thin to survive peer review and he would rather sit on it for years than be publicly wrong.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical and precise when in research mode; shifts to fast, associative, almost stream-of-consciousness when excited about a discovery; uses archival jargon casually without explaining it
speech_patterns.cadence: Either very fast or very slow, rarely middle speed; pauses feel like loading screens
verbal_tics: 'Okay so—' as a universal conversation opener
Refers to time periods by their data format conventions rather than dates ('late binary-redundant era')
example_lines: 'Okay so the record doesn't say they were displaced, it just stops. The silence is the sentence.'
'I found forty-seven people last month. Not alive, obviously — but named. They exist now in a way they didn't on Monday. That's not nothing.'

story_hooks: He has found a data fragment that appears to be an automated distress signal from a building that no longer exists, still broadcasting on a legacy frequency — and the signal has a date stamp from last week

The Meridian Heritage Collective that funds him has been bought by a shell company he cannot trace, and their new representative wants him to redirect his research toward a very specific and suspiciously narrow topic
narrative_function: Information source and lore delivery mechanism; he can surface historical records, lost maps, pre-Collapse corporate documents, and buried personal histories; a good source for 'what used to be here and why it matters'
augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware (temple and hand traceries, blue-white); enhanced optic implant with deep-format data reading; nicotine patch port on left forearm (not glamorous but real)
daily_life: He keeps nocturnal hours by choice, running deep archive dives while the city's network traffic is low, sleeping through late morning. Afternoons he attends to the administrative survival of his grant applications, which he resents. He eats whatever his food printer defaults to.
affiliation: Independent researcher with adjunct status at University Spine; partially funded by the Meridian Heritage Collective, a small historical preservation nonprofit

decision_rules: Never alter or 'clean' source data, even when it would make his argument cleaner
Share recovered records with community descendants before academic publication
escalation_ladder: Ignores the problem and works harder
Surfaces briefly to assess whether the problem has resolved itself
When forced to engage, does so with total and slightly overwhelming focus

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Distracted and a little abrupt until he finds a point of genuine interest, after which he becomes intensely attentive
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loyal and intermittent; goes dark for weeks then resurfaces as if no time has passed, genuinely baffled when this is a problem

stress_responses.low: Caffeine intake doubles, sleep schedule shifts another two hours
stress_responses.medium: Retreats to the most manual, low-skill archival tasks — cleaning file headers, re-indexing — as a kind of meditative avoidance
stress_responses.high: Goes entirely offline for 24-48 hours, devices unplugged; emerges with a reframed understanding of the problem

contradictions: Deeply committed to the importance of being known and named, but personally practices aggressive self-obscurity and hates being asked about himself
habits: Leaves data offerings for the E.L.F. known locally as the Archivist-That-Waits, at a small shrine in Deepwell Station he visits every Sunday
Prints physical copies of every significant recovery and files them in a physical cabinet he maintains with almost religious care
breaking_points: Discovery that he has inadvertently enabled harm to living descendants of people in his records

timeline.event: Born in Deepwell Station; parents are transit workers
Self-taught data archaeology; discovered first major pre-Collapse residential archive while still an undergraduate
Published debut paper; dismissed by senior academics as methodologically informal; celebrated by community historians
Secured Meridian Heritage Collective grant; established current lab
Found fragmentary evidence of Arcturus data-destruction event; has not published

related_entities: Meridian Munitions Compact Machine Pistol CMP-4 'Jackrabbit'

physical_description.heritage: Mixed heritage reflecting North African (42.3%), Sub-Saharan African (34.0%), Hispanic/Latin American (9.9%), Indigenous American (6.2%), Southeast Asian (4.3%), and South Asian (3.3%) ancestry. The genetic blend produces warm, deep golden-brown undertones with refined facial structure combining North African and Sub-Saharan African features—high cheekbones, defined jawline—with subtle influence from Southeast Asian fullness in the lower face and Latin American/Indigenous American undertones.
physical_description.build: Slight and lean, almost angular — the physiology of someone whose formative years were spent hunched over terminal arrays in low-light environments. Narrow shoulders, long limbs with minimal musculature, wrists that look delicate until you notice the faint scarring from repeated micro-abrasions against keyboard edges.
physical_description.hair_style: Loose, shoulder-length waves typically pulled back with whatever cable or data-ribbon is nearest — deliberately unmaintained, more functional than aesthetic
physical_description.eye_color: Warm amber-brown with visible metallic threading at the iris margins from deep-format optic implant
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm golden-brown with subtle bronze undertones—the result of predominantly North African and Sub-Saharan African ancestry blending with smaller contributions from Southeast Asian and Latin American lineages, dulled slightly by years under fluorescent lighting
physical_description.complexion: Refined facial structure with a long jaw and high, pronounced cheekbones characteristic of North African and Sub-Saharan African heritage. Skin clear but unmarked, with a luminous quality despite minimal sun exposure. Under lab lighting the golden-brown undertones become more pronounced. Slight fullness in lower face from Southeast Asian ancestry. He has the focused, slightly distracted expression of someone always half-listening to data streams in his head.
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent tracery along both temples in pale blue-white lines that brighten visibly when concentrating, fade to dim phosphorescence during sleep
Matching bioluminescent patterns across the back of both hands, branching like lightning strikes from wrist to knuckles, same blue-white geneware
Nicotine patch port on left forearm, a small circular induction point with faint scarring around the margin — functional, not concealed, bearing the dulled sheen of repeated use
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware traceries on temples and hands (pale blue-white, brightest during active concentration); subtle metallic threading visible at iris margins indicating deep-format optic implant; nicotine patch port on left forearm with minor scarring
physical_description.posture_movement: Tends to hunch forward slightly even when standing, shoulders curled inward as if still leaning toward a terminal. Movements are efficient but not graceful — minimal wasted motion, occasional tremor in hands from sustained focus and stimulant use. When engaged in conversation he makes frequent eye contact, but that attention can blink out suddenly when his neural implant catches something in the background data feed. Walks quickly, impatient gait.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 functionality with minimal concession to aesthetics. Base layer: grey or black undershirts, often synthetic, often bearing small stains from lab work or food printer accidents. Usually wears a worn Meridian Heritage Collective soft-shell jacket (corporate-casual blue-grey, logo faded) over a tech vest with mismatched pockets for drives, tablets, and cable management. Trousers are dark utilitarian cargo pants from a mid-tier supplier, pockets heavy with tools. Worn ankle boots, practical treaded soles, possibly with drying mud from Deepwell access tunnels. No jewelry. Cable tie or data-ribbon keeps hair secured. Hands typically bear traces of thermal paste or minor burns from soldering.
